headlines.text: Turning the clock back to 2026: Kevin Knight vs. Darby Allin went to battle over the AEW TNT Title, appearing on Dynamite, rated 7.64 ? a strong outing. It was the 140th time the AEW TNT Title had been on the line, a genuinely rare milestone for that title. In the same building where Knight first beat him, Allin started a brawl before the bell even rang, but Knight nailed him with the title belt behind the referee's back to retain ? closing in on becoming the first man to ten TNT Title defenses.

Flash back to 2020, when Eddie Kingston made their first appearance under the AEW banner against Cody, appearing on Dynamite, rated 7.99 ? a well-paced, entertaining battle. Kingston challenged TNT Champion Cody to a No Disqualification match after a heated confrontation ? a physical, high-stakes title opportunity that showcased Kingston's hard-hitting brawling style against one of the promotion's biggest stars
Turning the clock back to 2022: AEW welcomed Ashley D'Amboise for the first time against Britt Baker vs. Jamie Hayter vs. Skye Blue, appearing on Rampage, rated 4.71.

secondaries.text: Turning the clock back to 2023: Allin & Punk announced their arrival in style, headlining their very first AEW appearance as a team, appearing on Collision, rated 7.39 ? a strong outing.

Looking back to 2026, when Divine Dominion vs. Sisters Of Sin fought tooth and nail for the AEW Women's World Tag Team Titles in a No DQ match, appearing on Dynamite, rated 6.24. It was the 10th time the AEW Women's World Tag Team Titles had been on the line, a notable milestone for the title.

Turning the clock back to 2020: The Young Bucks vs. The Butcher and The Blade settled things in a Falls Count Anywhere match on Dynamite, rated 8.10 ? one of the better matches of the year in a physical tag team battle.
